purpose: Test whether the high score of the frozen three-column model is usual in a particular normal background. The background is explicitly fixed as columns 1 and 5 (one-based), disjoint from scoring columns 2,3,6. No patient attributes are interpreted clinically.
data: Only first-occurrence unique normal rows from train-set.csv until freeze; seed 42 reserves 20% for final calibration before any validation or estimator fitting.
reference_score: Normal-fit Yeo-Johnson + median and Q10-Q90 scaling on columns 2,3,6, then max(z2,0)*max(-z6,0)/(1+max(z3,0)). Historical directions, alpha and correction arose in part from course feedback.
subgroup_score: Fit a separate median and Q10-Q90 scaler to the two background columns. Take k nearest normal fitting records in the resulting Euclidean space. Assign each neighbor weight exp(-0.5*(distance/h)^2), h the furthest retained distance (all weights 1 when h=0). Estimate the local weighted empirical 99th percentile of frozen three-column normal scores. Shrink this quantile linearly toward the global fitting 99th percentile with coefficient n_eff/(n_eff+m) where n_eff=(sum w)^2/sum(w^2). Adjust the raw score by multiplying by global_q99/shrunken_local_q99. Set each method's final upper threshold on held-out normals at alpha=.005 and predict with strict >. Global and local weighted quantiles both use inverse-empirical-CDF convention.
validation: Use the original 1425 fitting normals in three outer folds (KFold shuffle seed 1126). For each fold reserve 25% of the other two-thirds as normal calibration (seed 800 + zero-based fold); fit on the rest and validate on the held-out fold. The 357 final normal calibration rows are never selected on. Report the original three-column score as a fixed control, plus the three local estimators.
stress: For every held-out recipient, find its 128 nearest fitting normals in background columns 1,5. Rank these neighbors by the smaller of their empirical ranks for high column 2 and low column 6. Draw the more-severe donor in the top ten percent of that joint rank, and its paired reference strictly below it in column 2 and above it in column 6, from the lower half of the joint rank. Perturb recipient columns 2,3,4,6 jointly by t*(donor-reference), retaining the recipient's two background values and the donor pair's four-coordinate change vector. Use fixed mild t=Uniform(0.45,0.85) and stronger t=Uniform(0.85,1.25), sharing each pair; seed 2126 + zero-based fold. If strict matched pairs do not exist after trying the extreme decile, omit that recipient from simulation only and record counts. For diagnosis, also report the subgroup of artificial scores within [0.5,1.5] times the *unadjusted* control threshold. This subset is not used for selection.
selection: Select only among the three prespecified subgroup candidates; the unadjusted frozen control is descriptive. Retain candidates with pooled normal FPR <=0.005; among those maximize mean of mild/strong simulated detection rates; ties use lower normal FPR then listed order. If none meet the limit, use smallest normal FPR then highest mean simulated detection, then listed order. Freeze one selected estimator and threshold before reading course test data. No test-driven choice of columns, groups, dimensions, weights or seeds.
assessment: Course evaluation for the frozen single candidate only, after saving scores without labels. The stress is an artificial within-background perturbation test, not independent evidence of disease recall.
